## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Satthapāṇi-sikkhāpada* ("Holding a knife") is the fifty-ninth training rule of the *sekhiya* section in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule regulates monastic decorum regarding teaching the Dhamma, specifically prohibiting a monk from teaching Dhamma to anyone holding a weapon or knife, unless that person is ill. An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral demonstrate that this training rule is preserved across virtually all extant Vinaya traditions [SuttaCentral]. In Pali literature, it is found in the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga*, *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha*, and both Parivāra collections [SuttaCentral]. Extensive cross-tradition parallels exist in Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese translations of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya vinayas [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus computational analysis reflects substantial intra-canonical textual reuse across 26 Pali texts (73 matching passages), sharing standardized legal and disciplinary formulas most extensively with neighboring *sekhiya* rules—especially Sekhiya 60 (§0.1–1.11), 65, 58, and 72—as well as the *Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi* [DharmaNexus].
